Before you see any data

Seal your bet.

Every decision is a bet on a future you can't fully see. Make yours now, before the data talks you into anything.

1 · The callBuild or don't?“Don't build” is a legal answer.
2 · The siteWhere?Denver · Phoenix · Dallas · Reno · Atlanta · Kansas City · Salt Lake City · Columbus
3 · The confidence___ %How sure are you? 50% means coin flip. 100% means you'd bet your job.

Write it down. Fold it. Don't open it until 01:55. Inspired by Annie Duke, Thinking in Bets.

01 · Product thinking

Clarity before code.

“You must not fool yourself — and you are the easiest person to fool.”Richard Feynman
Invert it · Charlie MungerDon’t ask “where should we build?” Ask “what would make this a $30M mistake?” If the math says you have to build, find the constraint that said so, and ask whether it’s real.

A national retailer serves 18 stores from one Chicago DC. Demand is shifting west. Should it spend $30M on a second DC?

Activity → Explore stores, DCs, and demand. Frame the decision.

FROM A SPECTRUM TO A PARTNERSHIP
INTUITIONOPTIMIZATION
NOT EITHER / OR. BOTH.
INTUITIONAsk the right question.
Choose meaningful inputs.

OPTIMIZATIONEvaluate trade-offs.
Respect constraints.

04 · Storytelling

The opening earns attention.

The Hero's Journey gives you the full arc. Micro-stories get to the point when you have 60 seconds.

THE LONG FORM

Hero's Journey

THE SHORT PITCH

Choose your opening

Inspired by Mike Adams, Seven Stories Every Salesperson Must Tell
INSIGHT“We assumed freight rates were the issue. It turns out our network design is the real problem.”
PROOF“Our model compared ___ networks. Opening ___ saves $___M a year and pays back in ___ years. Here is the one assumption that would flip it.”
ORIGIN“Last holiday season, our western stores ran out of stock while inventory sat hundreds of miles away. That is why we started rethinking our network.”
Fill the blanks with your own model’s numbers. Proof you can’t defend isn’t proof.

Activity → Pick an opening and deliver a 60-second executive pitch.

Flipped your callc²Sure at 90% and the evidence turned you? Score 0.81. Lower is better.
The real lessonProcess > outcome.A great decision can still lose. Judge how you decided, not how it turned out.
